- When sentiment is consistently low or negative (≤0.3), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 20-day moving average for stabilization.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model may overreact; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to prevent overcorrection.
- In low-sentiment periods, model often fails to capture mean reversion; force a 3–5 day lagged mean reversion adjustment if price deviates >2σ from 30-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, model tends to ignore it; add 1–2% downward bias to avoid “overconfident” upward bias.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings >0.25), model overfits short-term noise; use 7-day smoothed sentiment as a dampening factor for forecast adjustments.
